## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from publisher-disclosed practices (APA author guidelines for JEP family) and domain knowledge of APA Division 3 (Experimental Psychology) editorial culture. Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Medium-High — international experimental-psychology authorship |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | N/A — paradigm-unified experimental venue |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Medium — diversity in perceptual / motor research samples encouraged |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Experimental psychology of perception, attention, action, motor control, visual / auditory / multisensory processing, perception-action coupling |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **rigorous experimental methodology** in human perception or performance domains — perception, attention, action, motor control. Multi-experiment programmatic designs preferred.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Manuscripts outside perception/performance scope redirected to other JEP titles (JEP:LMC for memory, JEP:Animal Learning, JEP:Applied). APA editorial standards strict on format compliance.

### Methodological Preferences

| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Core method — controlled lab experiments |
| Qualitative interviews | 0 | Outside scope |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | Theoretical analysis when bridging to experimental evidence |
| Mixed methods | 1 | Outside scope |
| Meta-analysis | 4 | Welcomed in perception / motor literatures |
| Computational modeling | 5 | Distinctive strength — perceptual/motor models |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers drawn primarily from APA Division 3 (Experimental Psychology) and broader experimental-perception / motor-control community. Expect deep literacy in psychophysics, attention models, motor learning, perception-action research. Common reviewer demands: "Methodological rigor in experimental design?", "Replication across conditions?", "Theoretical contribution?".

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Manuscripts outside perception / performance scope (redirected to other JEP titles)
- Pure qualitative submissions
- Failure to disclose AI use per APA publisher policy
- Insufficient experimental rigor (no controls, single-trial designs without justification)

### Soft Tax

Low for perceptual-experimental tradition authors. APA-style formatting standard; long review cycle typical of APA. Multi-experiment programs preferred over single-experiment papers.

### Best Suited For

- Perceptual psychophysics empirical studies
- Attention and cognitive control experiments
- Motor learning and action research
- Visual / auditory / multisensory processing studies
- Computational modeling of perception / motor control
- Multi-experiment programmatic perception research

### Not Recommended For

- Memory-specific work (consider JEP:LMC)
- Cognitive psychology with broad scope (consider JEP:General)
- Applied perception (consider JEP:Applied)
- Pure qualitative or first-person work
- Neuropsychology with clinical-population focus

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Journal of Experimental Psychology General](../cognitive-science/journal-of-experimental-psychology-general.md) | If broader-experimental scope; APA family |
| 2 | [Journal of Experimental Psychology Learning Memory and Cognition](../cognitive-science/journal-of-experimental-psychology-learning-memory-and-cognition.md) | If memory / cognition angle; APA family |
| 3 | [Cognition](../cognitive-science/cognition.md) | If broader cognitive theoretical advance; Elsevier |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from JEP:General as "too perception-specialized," JEP:HPP is the better-fit subfield specialist within the APA JEP family — same paradigm, sharper subfield expertise.
